# hands/mail

the only holder of Teeny's AgentMail key.

## How to call it

Run it from the repository root with your shell (exec) tool: `hands/mail <verb> [flags]`.

- A verb that takes a body reads one JSON object from stdin. Everything else is flags.
- It prints one JSON object on stdout. Exit 0 is success. Exit 2 is a refusal by a rule, the guard or a cap: read the `rule` and `reason`, and do not retry it unchanged. Any other exit is an error.
- Secrets belong to the hand; you never see them and never pass one.
- The hand runs the guard, its caps and `DRY_RUN` itself. `DRY_RUN` is on unless the box turned it off; under it an acting verb checks every rule and sends nothing. Do not try to go around the hand, and do not look for another way to do what it refused.

## Side effects

- Acting (side effects in the world, each goes through the guard and the caps): reply; send; label
- Job (writes state or calls the core): ingest [--max N] [--no-offer]; queue [--status S], mark ID --status S [--note T], requests [--status S]
- Operator only (never call): contacts add EMAIL --kind vendor|winner|collaborator [--note T], contacts list, contacts remove EMAIL
- Read only: whoami; list [--unread] [--max N] [--label L], get ID, thread ID; codes [--since-minutes N] [--from-domain D]

## Verbs

| Verb | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `whoami` | R | `/auth/me` and whether its inbox scope `matches` `AGENTMAIL_INBOX`. |
| `list [--unread] [--max N] [--label L]`, `get ID`, `thread ID` | R | Recent mail (1 min), a message (10 min), a thread (2 min). |
| `codes [--since-minutes N] [--from-domain D]` | R | Verification codes (4 to 8 capitals and digits with a digit, near "code", "verify", "OTP", "sign in", ...; a year is not a code) and verification links from mail received in the last N minutes (30). |
| `ingest [--max N] [--no-offer]` | J | Reads new mail since the `mail_cursor` timestamp into `mail_messages`, unique on message id. |
| `queue [--status S]`, `mark ID --status S [--note T]`, `requests [--status S]` | J | The intake (statuses as `x_mentions`), what became of a message, the build requests. |
| `reply` | A | `{message_id, body}`. |
| `send` | A | `{to, subject, body}`; `to` is an address or up to 5. |
| `label` | A | `{message_id, add?, remove?}`. |
| `contacts add EMAIL --kind vendor\|winner\|collaborator [--note T]`, `contacts list`, `contacts remove EMAIL` | O | Who Teeny may mail first. |

Kinds: R = read: no side effect beyond its read cache; A = acting: posts, sends, pays or opens something in the world; O = operator-only: the operator runs it, never you; J = job: writes state or calls the core, says nothing to anyone; scheduled jobs run it, you do not.

Verbs named in the hand's source: `codes`, `contacts`, `get`, `ingest`, `list`, `mark`, `queue`, `requests`, `thread`, `whoami`.

Flags named in the hand's source: `--from-domain`, `--kind`, `--label`, `--max`, `--no-offer`, `--note`, `--since-minutes`, `--status`, `--unread`.

For one verb's exact flags, run `DRY_RUN=1 hands/mail <verb> --help`. The full account is in docs/hands.md.
